newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian gas, heating prices soar under reforms.
newsitem.headline: Romanian gas, heating prices soar under reforms.

text.p: Romanian authorities boosted prices for gas and heating by up to five times on Thursday as part of market reforms, a move certain to worsen already soaring inflation and hit hard-pressed consumers.
Under measures approved by Western lenders, heating prices trebled and natural gas prices went up five times.
Adevarul newspaper said the increases jacked the average annual family gas bill to the equivalent of $380. Average monthly salaries stand at about $70.
Government officials acknowledge that the rises, intended to bring energy rates in line with world prices, would generate further temporary rises in inflation.
Monthly inflation last month hit a record 30.7 percent and price rises for the first quarter stand at 76.5 percent.
Romania's budget forecasts annual inflation of 90 percent in 1997 against 56.9 percent last year, but Western experts say the figure is probably out of reach.
Under market reforms launched in February by the new centrist government, prices for fuel, electricity and staple goods were increased by more than 50 percent.
Gas and heating increases were postponed until May to cushion the impact on living standards during the winter.
The reforms helped to secure resumption of International Monetary Fund credits last month, with Romania to receive a total of $430 million over the next 13 months.
Romania counts on Russian imported gas for some 30 percent of its consumption, or about 24 billion cubic metres. Domestic gas production is estimated at 17.1 billion for 1997.
